claims.claim: Veracode's 2025 GenAI Code Security Report tested over 100 large language models across Java, Python, C#, and JavaScript to see if advanced AI systems can write secure code.
claims.quote: In our new **2025 GenAI Code Security Report**, we tested over **100 large language models** across **Java, Python, C#, and JavaScript**. The goal? To see if today’s most advanced AI systems can write **secure** code.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: 45% of code samples failed security tests and introduced OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.
claims.quote: 45% of code samples failed security tests and introduced OWASP Top 10 security vulnerabilities into the code.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Java was the riskiest language, with a 72% security failure rate across tasks.
claims.quote: **Java** was the riskiest language, with a **72% security failure****rate**across tasks.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Python had a 38% security failure rate, JavaScript 43%, and C# 45%.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Cross-Site Scripting (CWE-80) was a frequent issue; AI tools failed to defend against it in 86% of relevant code samples.
claims.quote: In fact, one of the most frequent issues was:**Cross-Site Scripting (CWE-80)**: AI tools failed to defend against it in 86**%** of relevant code samples.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Newer or larger models improved functional or syntactically correct code but not secure code; security performance stayed flat regardless of model size or training.
claims.quote: While the models got better at writing **functional** or syntactically correct code, they were **no better at writing secure code**. Security performance remained **flat,**regardless of model size or training sophistication.
